texts: In a bidirectional cavopulmonary shunt, systemic venous blood is diverted to the lungs, reducing the volume load on the single ventricle: B.
The ventricle no longer pumps the pulmonary blood flow as well as the systemic, so its work falls while oxygenation improves.

The SVC blood that reaches the lungs is the most desaturated, the SVC must be clamped or shunted while it is joined, and without hepatic venous blood in the lungs pulmonary arteriovenous malformations can form.
Aortopulmonary collaterals add to the volume load and may be coiled.
In the picture, once the chimney is bent to the money pipe, the one engine room's fan slows, relieved.
Memory hook: the astronaut takes half the load off the single fan.
